question.text: Mr. Karthik Menon, a senior analyst at Ganga Capital (the Manager of 'Ganga Mid-Market Fund II', a Cat II AIF), wishes to personally invest in the scheme he works on. What is the minimum investment amount applicable to him under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: INR 25 lakh, as he is an employee of the Investment Manager
INR 1 crore, same as all regular investors
INR 10 crore, applicable to key personnel
Employees are prohibited from investing in their own managed fund

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 10(c) carves out a lower minimum of INR 25 lakh for employees or directors of the AIF / Investment Manager investing in personal capacity. For all other investors, the minimum is INR 1 crore (not applicable to Accredited Investors under the 2021 amendment). Social Impact Fund individuals have a separate INR 2 lakh minimum. The Trap: Option B applies the general investor floor. Option C confuses with SSF's INR 10 cr investor minimum. Option D is plainly wrong — employee participation is expressly envisaged and is even encouraged as alignment. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A asks the INR 1 cr base threshold. XIX-C adds the employee carve-out. This is a favourite compliance exam question (III-A/C).
